historical_reviews.deepseek: The typed Power Supply SDR query is useful discovery, but the second filtered view is truncated, credentials are exposed and neither command proves the platform's PSU-to-record map or all three required views.
historical_reviews.gpt_v2: Correctly treats power-supply identity and expected state as owner inputs and forbids PSU, PMBus and power-control writes. This review also separates aggregate PSU state from rail telemetry.
historical_reviews.duplicate_search: No duplicate code variant exists; adjacent fan and GPU-temperature rows do not define PSU coverage.
historical_reviews.v3_1: ED-35 requires per-member evidence for 1~N; ED-36 makes installed power topology and state semantics readiness inputs; ED-38 preserves power/log state and engineer verdict ownership.

original_test_intent: Validate every installed PSU status channel, its stable sensor identity and description, the intended presence/input/output/fault state semantics and consistency across SDR, Sensor List and BMC Web.
original_method: The power owner enumerates installed PSU bays and feeds, maps each 1~N member to exact SDR records and Web rows, defines aggregate-state versus rail-reading expectations, then automation passively gathers complete IPMI evidence for a per-PSU comparison.
manual_activity: The power/platform owner defines installed PSU bays, feed and redundancy context, exact status semantics and Web mappings, then reviews every member. No PSU hot service, feed switching or power-state change is part of this passive check.
required_inputs: Installed PSU count, bay order, model/firmware and independent AC-feed topology
Exact 1~N applicability and per-bay SDR record/entity and BMC-Web mapping
Definition of aggregate presence/input-lost/output-lost/predictive-failure state versus voltage/current/power rails
Expected normal states, numeric ranges/units/tolerance, absent/standby semantics and update interval
BMC/SDR/PSU firmware and PMBus bridge versions
System load and redundancy assumptions required for interpretation
Protected OOB credential path and complete-evidence collector
Power/thermal aborts and independent recovery owner
safety_requirements: Use the exact row/variant and enumerate every required PSU rather than passing one representative bay
Do not infer PSU health solely from one aggregate SDR or one numeric rail
Retain complete SDR and Sensor List output; PSU/STATUS filters and the 40-line cap are derived views only
Never issue PMBus writes, PSU resets, power commands, feed switching or hot-remove actions
Do not clear logs; protect credentials and preserve SEL/power evidence
Stop on input/output loss, predictive failure, rail anomaly, thermal rise, BMC instability or loss of independent recovery
agent_execution_scope: Verify exact source identity and installed PSU topology
Capture complete read-only SDR and Sensor List inventories plus typed Power Supply records
Resolve owner-approved per-bay aggregate and rail sensors
Build per-member SDR/Sensor parity and prepare exact Web rows for operator confirmation
Correlate passive PSU redundancy, rails, thermal, SEL and platform health
Perform no PMBus/power write, physical service, fault injection or verdict
engineer_actions: Approve PSU bay/feed membership and applicability
Define each status and rail criterion including absent/standby behavior
Confirm BMC-Web mapping and redundancy context
Review every PSU result and issue the overall verdict

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: `sdr type 'Power Supply'` is a relevant passive view, but the broad PSU/STATUS filter capped at 40 lines is incomplete, exposes credentials and cannot establish bay identity or Sensor List/Web parity.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Via secret-safe approved OOB access, retain complete SDR and Sensor List inventories and the typed Power Supply view; map exact owner-enumerated bays and compare aggregate states and rail readings separately against specification and Web rows.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: STATUS_PSU 1~N, the BMC-Web check, three criteria and 3/3-minute estimates remain; PSU count, topology and expected states are not invented.

modernized_recommendation.status: REQUIRES PSU TOPOLOGY AND STATE-MATRIX PACKAGE
modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Create a bay/feed-to-sensor matrix, capture complete passive inventories at an identified load state, compare aggregate state and rail telemetry by member, and reconcile exact Web rows without disturbing power.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds the missing power-topology and state semantics while avoiding the generic destructive log clear.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: A typed SDR list may omit vendor records, while a broad status filter can include unrelated power sensors; aggregate `Present/OK` cannot replace voltage/current/power acceptance.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Passive reads are low impact, but an incorrect normal-state interpretation can hide redundancy loss or an unsafe rail condition.

project_override_considerations: N+1, 2N, shared-feed and standby PSU designs require project-specific expected-state matrices. Unpopulated bays must be explicitly marked not applicable rather than treated as missing failures.
expected_evidence: Per-bay aggregate and rail SDR record/entity/unit/state/value/freshness plus Web mapping
Versioned PSU/power specification and load context
Complete redacted SDR, Sensor List and typed Power Supply outputs with status/timestamps
Timestamped Web evidence with SEL, rail, thermal and platform health

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The source consistently requests PSU sensor-list agreement across three views. It is underspecified and contains a generic destructive log-clear step, but it does not contradict its PSU target.

blocked_analysis.analysis: PSU status monitoring and a passive evidence path are identifiable. Installed topology, state semantics and numeric criteria are project-supplied readiness inputs under ED-36.

review_improvement: Converts STATUS_PSU 1~N into a bay/feed-aware matrix, prevents aggregate state from substituting for rail health and bars the passive sensor case from expanding into power manipulation.
independent_technical_reasoning: Power Supply SDRs may report discrete presence, input loss, output loss, redundancy and predictive failure independently from voltage, current or power readings. Those signals are not interchangeable, and their expected state depends on installed bays, feeds and load. Complete inventories plus an owner-approved topology allow passive correlation across IPMI and Web without exercising the power path.
